desc: The digital assistant supports policy staff in answering parliamentary questions by searching public sources

name: Digital identification and verification
authority: Ministry of Justice and Security, Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations
desc: Public authorities in the Netherlands have explored digital identification methods to improve security, efficiency and user experience in public services. This research initiative examined the potential use of biometric identifiers, such as facial recognition, within government contexts.

name: Dutch cycling intelligence
desc: The Dutch Cycling Intelligence programme developed the Digital Twin “Atlas of the Accessible City” to provide data-driven insights into urban accessibility and cycling infrastructure.

name: DutchCycling - Cycling Lifestyle AI
desc: Streets in many cities remain dominated by cars, limited greenery, and fragmented cycling infrastructure, making it difficult for residents and planners to imagine what a healthier, more bicycle-friendly street could look like in practice.

name: E-Discovery - automatic classifcation of incoming and outgoing emails
desc: In 2016, the Nationaal Archief started a study into the possibilities of E-discovery within information management. As part of this research, in collaboration with the ICT Implementation Organisation (ICTU), a prototype has been developed that automatically classifies incoming and outgoing e-mails.

name: Early school leavers in the municipality of Amersfoort - Estimation of students at risk
desc: The municipality of Amersfoort and Dordrecht use an algorithm to estimate which students are at risk of becoming early school leavers.

name: Enforcement of social policy laws with AI
authority: UWV, SVB, the Tax And Customs Administration, DUO, Justid, CJIB and RDW
desc: AI to monitor the enforcement of the social security laws checking for fraud.

name: Excess Material Exchange (EME)
desc: Various organizations are exploring the possibilities of exchanging residual materials among themselves. With the help of AI, supply and demand are linked together and a trading platform is created to close the residual flows circle of the organizations.

name: Firework nuisance detection system - AI to determine if bangs are firework
desc: Dutch municipalities face recurring public order and safety issues linked to illegal fireworks, particularly during evenings and festive periods, placing strain on enforcement capacity and generating resident complaints.

name: FlowCube - a picture of the traffic of cyclists, vehicles and pedestrians
desc: The aim of the development of this system is to get a picture of the traffic of cyclists, vehicles and pedestrians. This is done by means of compact video and AI modules, also called the FlowCube. The image recognition in FlowCube detects cyclists, cars and pedestrians.

name: Forensic Image Recognition (FIRE) -  Recognition of containers that have illegal cargo
desc: The Netherlands Forensic Institute (NFI) is best known for the most visible part of forensic research. The men and women in white suits. “But our field of work goes much further than that,” says Lisanne van Dijk. In principle, we have three core tasks.

name: From A to B: Generalizing the mathematics of artificial neural networks (ANNs) to biological neural networks (BNNs)
desc: Understanding why and when neural network models learn effectively remains a fundamental scientific challenge with implications for both artificial intelligence and neuroscience.

name: GEO reference of documents - Gaining more insight into data on nitrogen emissions and soil pollution
desc: Bolesian has developed an application for the province of Gelderland with which large amounts of unstructured information and data can be analyzed. The focus is on gaining more insight into data on nitrogen emissions and soil pollution.

name: GPT-NL - A language model for the Dutch language and culture
authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate
desc: Many widely used language models are developed outside the Netherlands and may not adequately reflect Dutch language use, legal requirements, or national priorities around privacy, cultural context, and technological independence.

name: Geniq -  reports wait times
desc: Calculates, analyzes, and reports wait times, so that an institution always has up-to-date insights.

name: Goochem - a pioneering interactive chatbot created as a marketing tool to bring culture closer to young people
desc: As a result, Amsterdam Marketing and the City of Amsterdam have launched Goochem, a new chatbot, available via Facebook Messenger.

name: Good Public Space for Walking pilot in multiple dutch Municipalities
authority: Municipalities of Den Haag, Groningen, Nijmegen, Rotterdam
desc: Across many towns and cities, public spaces are designed with certain assumptions about how people will move, stop and interact, yet the way these places are actually used often differs from what planners intended.

name: Graasdierpremie - Use of drones in counting animals
authority: Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority (NVWA)
desc: Nature conservation by automatically monitoring animal distribution and animal abundance. Typically, such conservation tasks are performed manually on foot or after an aerial recording from a manned aircraft. Such manual approaches are expensive, slow and labor intensive.

name: HKV Eye - Line in Water
desc: With HKVEYE ('a new organism on the dike'), HKV Lijn develops extra eyes in water to inspect dikes better and easier. HKVEYE looks in detail at the condition of the dike.

name: Hansken - Recognizing images of narcotics in digital seizure
desc: While investigating serious crimes, the police frequently seize data carriers such as mobile phones, computers, and hard drives in their search for incriminating evidence. However, the sheer volume of data often makes it impossible to manually review every device.

name: IBEACON LIVING LAB
desc: Amsterdam's Beacon Mile is the world's first beacon-guided city walk designed to inform tourists during their exploration of the city.

name: IVORY – ‘AI for Vision Zero in Road Safety’
authority: Delft University of Technology Faculty of Technology, Policy and Management
desc: Achieving major reductions in road fatalities requires more than isolated technical improvements, as road safety depends on the interaction between vehicles, infrastructure, human behaviour, governance, and public trust.

name: Identifying people at risk of falling into large debts
desc: People at risk of defaulting into large debts automatically surface

name: Improve data quality with AI - Machine learning to improve the data quality of registrations
authority: Municipality of The Hague and Phinion Data Engineering.
desc: The services of the municipality of The Hague run on data registrations. The quality of the registrations can have consequences for the quality of the service. In this pilot, AI (machine learning) was used with the aim of analyzing, monitoring and continuously improving the data quality of the registrations.

name: Infobox criminal and unexplained assets (iCOV)
authority: Public Prosecutor's Office, the National Police, the Tax Authorities, Customs, the FIOD and the Financial Intelligence Unit, the Social Affairs and Employment Inspectorate (Investigation Directorate), the Intelligence and Investigation Service of the Environment and Transport Inspectorate (ILT-IOD), the Intelligence and Investigation Service of the Dutch Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority (NVWA-IOD), the Media Commissioner
desc: System provides insight into the assets of individuals and companies based on risk factors. An example is analyzing suspicious transactions in Rotterdam-Zuid.

name: Inspection bridges with drones
authority: Ministry of Instrastructures and market parties
desc: Instead of human capacity, drones are used to inspect bridges and viaducts.

name: Intelligent traffic control systems (I-VRI's) - Better traffic flow
desc: The province of Gelderland has replaced the existing traffic lights with intelligent traffic control systems (iVRIs) at 8 intersections in Arnhem and Velp. These new installations ensure better flow. The iVRI's use mobile data from road users.

name: LAA - Address quality in Personal Records Database (BRP)
desc: The Dutch Ministry of Interior uses data analysis to achieve pattern recognition and to search for incorrect addressing based on this. The aim is to put the BRP in order and ultimately contribute to the fight against fraud.

name: LOQUI - participation by speech
desc: Digital public services increasingly rely on text-based interfaces, which creates significant barriers for people with language deficits, low literacy levels, visual impairments or limited digital skills, including new Dutch citizens and status holders.

name: Loting illegally buried cadavers with drones -  Use of drones to detect illegaly buried cadavers
authority: Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority (NVW
desc: The Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority needed a faster and more accurate way to identify sites where animal cadavers may have been buried illegally, since manual inspection over large areas is resource-intensive and can delay enforcement action.

name: MELISSA - Mobile Artificial Intelligence Solution for Diabetes Adaptive Care
desc: Effective diabetes management requires continuous adjustment of insulin therapy and monitoring of complications, yet many patients lack personalised, data-driven support between clinical visits.

name: MPAT – Mobility Policy Auto Tuner Pilot in Amsterdam
desc: Amsterdam’s ambition to reduce transport emissions requires sophisticated tools to understand and influence modal shift towards low-carbon mobility. The MPAT pilot supports this goal by providing a data-driven engine to optimise shared micro-mobility policies.

name: Movable Traffic Predictor
desc: The aim of this project is to develop a new type of traffic forecaster, based on AI, that can predict traffic up to about 1 hour ahead.

name: Nexus -  speech-operated expert system
authority: Brightlands Techruption, OU (CAROU), UM (BISS), Police NL (iLAB)
desc: Nexus is a speech-operated expert system that provides the Community Police Officers with a detailed briefing of recent incidents in their neighbourhood.

name: Object Detection Kit Amsterdam - Automatic detection of garbage
desc: Amsterdam introduced the Object Detection Kit to address a highly visible and operationally demanding urban-management issue: waste placed incorrectly in public space, especially near underground containers, was affecting street cleanliness and requiring frequent reporting and intervention.

name: One and a half meter monitor - Monitor which automatically calculates the distance between people
desc: Amsterdam introduced the 1.5 metre monitor during the COVID-19 pandemic to support enforcement of public-health guidance on social distancing in busy public spaces.

name: Outdoor Mobility Digital Twin at TU Delft
desc: The Technical University of Delft developed a digital twin of its campus environment to analyse and manage pedestrian and cyclist flows during the COVID-19 pandemic. Managing crowd density in public spaces became critical to ensure safety and compliance with health measures.

name: PRORAIL: Rail trespassers prediction
desc: ProRail aimed to improve the safety and efficiency of the Dutch rail network by using operational data to anticipate risks and optimise infrastructure management.

name: Parking control in various Dutch municipalities - Parking control by means of scan cars
authority: Municipality of Amsterdam (Parking, Team Analysis & Advice), the Hague, Rotterdam and Utrecht
desc: The IT team of four municipalities in the Netherlands (Amsterdam, The Hague, Rotterdam and Utrecht) developed a Parking control tool by means of scan cars. The scan cars are equipped with cameras and drive past parking spaces in the city.

name: Passer-by count
desc: City centres increasingly require reliable insights into pedestrian flows to support economic development, urban planning and public safety.

name: Pilot Youth Policy Rotterdam - Influencing factors socio-emotional development of young people
authority: Municipality of Rotterdam, TNO and BZK
desc: By linking datasets and using a combination of statistical methods and machine learning, we explore which factors determine the socio-emotional development of young people.

name: Poverty prevention - Identification of poverty and debt early
authority: Brightlands Techruption, CBS, municipality of Heerlen, CZ, Maastricht University, TNO
desc: Early signs of financial vulnerability are often missed because relevant data is distributed across multiple public agencies that cannot easily share information without infringing privacy regulations.

name: Predict which residents have a higher risk of care or debt problems in Twenterand (SyRI)
desc: At least 25 municipalities use predictive systems and algorithms to, for example, detect welfare fraud, predict where potentially subversive crime takes place and to be able to help citizens with debts in time. Risk profiling is under a magnifying glass.

name: Prediction of young people engagement in undesirable behaviour (Pilot Apeldoorn Youth)
desc: The municipality of Apeldoorn explored this pilot to address concerns about youth-related nuisance and other forms of undesirable behaviour in public space, with the aim of identifying where preventive action might be most needed.

name: Prevention of Diabetic Foot Syndrome
desc: Diabetic Foot Syndrome represents a major public health concern, frequently leading to hospitalisation and lower-limb amputation if not detected at an early stage.

name: Pro-Kid used for risk assessment by the Dutch police
desc: Since 2011, the Dutch police have used ProKid to support early identification of children and young people considered at risk of reoffending, informing preventive interventions by police and youth care services.

name: Project Jurisprudence Robot -  AI tool to support prosecutors and investigators
desc: Public prosecutors and investigators face growing volumes of legal material and case law, making it increasingly difficult to identify relevant jurisprudence efficiently and consistently.

name: Public Eye: AI crowd monitoring system in Amsterdam
desc: The City of Amsterdam developed Public Eye to support crowd management in busy public spaces such as Arena Boulevard, Marineterrein and Dam Square, where high visitor numbers can create safety risks and congestion.

name: RWS - Machine learning for road accident predictions
authority: Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management of the Netherlands
desc: Rijkswaterstaat operates a 24-hour incident-management service in which traffic managers monitor extensive real-time information across more than 15 screens, creating a demanding environment in which accident risks can be difficult to identify early and inspectors may not always be optimally positioned to respond…

name: Rain radar Rijnmond - Prediction of rain to prevent flooding and damage
desc: The Rijnmond rain radar measures and predicts precipitation in the region very locally. This helps prevent flooding and damage.

name: Reference Index Recherche Onderzoeken en Subjecten - Detection of unusual transactions
desc: Law enforcement agencies must efficiently identify suspicious financial transactions that may be linked to ongoing criminal investigations while operating within strict legal frameworks.

name: Remote sensing for monitoring nature reserves on the Frisian Wadden Islands
desc: The aim of this project was to test the feasibility of models that monitor vegetation with annual frequency based on satellite data. These models are optimized by means of machine learning techniques.

name: Reporting issues in public space
desc: When someone encounters rubbish or a maintenance issue on the street or in a park, they can report this to the municipality via an online reporting system. A dangerous traffic situation or disturbance from people or cafes can also be reported.

name: Rijkswaterstaat vital assets - Predictive maintenance on bridges
authority: Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management
desc: Using data to predict when maintenance should be carried out on bridges.

name: Road safety model Rotterdam - Predictive model for road accidents
desc: The Municipality of Rotterdam faces similar challenges to other large cities in managing road safety across a dense and diverse transport network.

name: Road safety model The Hague - Providing a risk score for all road sections and intersections
desc: Urban road authorities require proactive tools to reduce traffic accidents and prioritise safety interventions across complex road networks. The Municipality of The Hague developed a road safety model to assess and compare risk levels for all road sections and intersections within the city.

name: Roboat - an autonomous fleet for Amsterdam
authority: Amsterdam Institute for Advanced Metropolitan Solutions (AMS)
desc: Amsterdam’s canal network presents opportunities for innovative transport and urban services, yet managing congestion, waste collection and logistics in dense waterways is complex.

name: Rotterdam created digital twin to improve urban planning
desc: Urban planning in Rotterdam requires balancing growth, sustainability, and resilience, yet fragmented data limited predictive analysis and cross-domain optimisation.

name: Rotterdam – Improving the usage of rooftops
desc: The Municipality of Rotterdam needed a better understanding of how the city’s extensive stock of flat rooftops could contribute to urban sustainability goals, including water storage, green space creation and energy generation.

name: SIA - Notifications public space
desc: Municipalities receive large numbers of citizen reports about problems in public space, such as damage, nuisance or maintenance issues, and these notifications must be classified and routed to the appropriate department before action can begin.

name: Scan car for checking group formation and complying with corona measures
desc: During the COVID-19 pandemic, the municipality of Rotterdam needed ways to monitor compliance with public-health measures in urban space, particularly rules concerning group formation and distancing.

name: Sia - Online notification system of the municipality of Amsterdam
desc: SIA is an online notification system of the municipality of Amsterdam. Reports can be made in the following situations: If something needs to be made or cleaned up on the street or in a park, in case of a dangerous traffic situation or nuisance of persons and restaurants.

name: Signalen - AI Categorisation of Public Space Reports
authority: City of Amsterdam and other dutch municipalities
desc: Municipalities receive large volumes of reports from residents concerning issues in public space, such as waste, infrastructure damage or nuisance, which must be routed quickly to the correct department. Manual triage is time-consuming and can delay resolution.

name: Skendy - Multilingual Chatbot supporting Ukrainian refugees in the City of Amsterdam
desc: Newly arrived refugees often face significant barriers in understanding administrative requirements, particularly when dealing with unfamiliar languages and complex bureaucratic processes. In the City of Amsterdam, Ukrainian refugees required accessible support to manage official communications and documentation.

name: Smart Cameras - Analyzing road situations
desc: Smart cameras that can 'read' the situation on the road, making opening and closing rush-hour lanes faster, easier and safer.

name: Smart Dementia project
desc: The eHealth technology (a wristwatch and app with which the whereabouts of the patients can be traced) is used to provide elderly people with Alzheimer more freedom. The technology enables the nurses and the institution to trace the elderly better, thus giving them more freedom to move around.

name: Smart Street Scan really sets up municipal services differently
desc: Municipalities need to keep public spaces clean, yet litter and other waste in streets and public areas are often detected only after complaints or routine inspections, which can delay action and make municipal services less efficient.

name: Smart decision aid - Determining if a case is a scam or not
desc: The National Internet Reporting Centre receives 42,000 reports of buying and selling fraud every year. In about 10,000 cases, after studying a police officer, it turns out that this is not a criminal offence. The 'smart decision aid' helps determine whether this is a scam and links this directly back to the declarant.

name: Smart enforcement cameras - Enforcement of drivers driving through red road crosses
desc: In order to detect road users who ignore red crosses, and to reduce the number of violations, the Public Prosecutor's Office and Rijkswaterstaat have started a trial with enforcement using smart cameras along the A28 motorway near Amersfoort.

name: Smart lampposts for combating burglaries - Detection of suspicious movements and audio
desc: The Municipality of Rotterdam has installed smart lampposts in the Lombardijen district to combat burglaries. Sensors record suspicious movements and microphones hear if a window is being tapped.

name: Smart sensor waste containers
desc: Sensors are installed in waste containers to measure how full the bins are. The 'filling degree meter' transmits the position every hour. This information is used to look at when the container can best be emptied. Drivers can see on a tablet which route to take next.

name: Speaker Tracking in Time and Space
authority: Dutch Police, with Speech lab B.V.
desc: Spraaklab develops AI technology that can mostly disassemble and label the speech of the different speakers. This is useful for the police, for example, when analyzing audio recordings.

name: Spike - Energy Pilot Project in Amsterdam
desc: In Amsterdam, achieving climate goals requires scalable solutions that reduce building energy consumption while enabling participation in local energy communities. Many buildings operate inefficiently due to static control systems and limited integration with renewable energy sources.

name: SyRi - Detect welfare fraud
authority: Ministry of Social Affairs and Employment
desc: SyRi was introduced by the Dutch government in 2014 to address a longstanding administrative challenge: municipalities wanted a more systematic way to identify possible welfare fraud and misuse of public benefits across fragmented public-sector datasets.

name: Tackling undermining using AI
desc: More than 300 professionals now use the 'Report a Suspicion' platform of digital transformation agency Milvum. With a mobile app and web portal, Milvum can pass on suspicions of undermining - such as illegal prostitution or drug production - directly to the right people at the municipality.

name: The Hague Digital Twin
desc: The Municipality of The Hague is developing a digital twin within the Scheveningen Living Lab to better understand and manage urban dynamics, particularly in high-traffic coastal areas. Urban planners face challenges in monitoring real-time conditions and anticipating congestion, especially during peak periods.

name: The Hague and The Routing Company develop on-demand public transit service
desc: Fixed-route public transport in low-density neighbourhoods often suffers from low occupancy rates and limited flexibility, resulting in operational inefficiencies and reduced service attractiveness.

name: The Hague uses AI to reduce laughing gas nuisance
desc: The Hague Municipality tested the possibility of using smart artificial intelligence cameras to detect laughing gas abuse in the boulevard of Scheveningen.

name: The Refinery: AI in investigation support
desc: The Refinery (Dutch: De Raffinaderij) is an artificial intelligence and data-analysis facility developed by the Dutch National Police to enhance investigative capabilities. The platform enables investigators to access, interpret, and visualize large volumes of police data drawn from diverse sources.

name: The Sensing Project for risk assessment and profiling by the Roermond police
desc: The Roermond police developed the Sensing Project to address recurring pickpocketing and shoplifting in a shopping district, focusing on patterns described as “mobile banditry”. The operational objective was to identify vehicles and groups considered likely to commit offences and deploy patrols more efficiently.

name: The smart bridge
desc: The province of South Holland has an important role in the traffic flow within the region by operating and maintaining more than 100 bridges. Smart ICT solutions offer new opportunities to link up-to-date traffic information with live shipping information via sensors and algorithms.

name: Tracing potential victims of human trafficking and labour exploitation with AI
desc: Labour exploitation and human trafficking are difficult to detect because warning signs are often hidden within ordinary-looking financial activity, making traditional investigation methods slow and resource-intensive.

name: Tree Monitor - Detecting illegal logging
authority: Province of Gelderland, NEO, Wageningen Environmental Research
desc: Since December 2017, the province of Gelderland has had an additional tool for detecting illegal logging: the tree monitor. Satellite images from different years are compared with each other, if trees have disappeared somewhere, the map indicates this.

name: Use of scan cars for underground containers - Determining type of waste
desc: Municipal waste management services struggle with contamination of waste streams when incorrect materials are deposited in underground containers, leading to higher processing costs and reduced recycling rates.

name: Using AI to measure accessibility
desc: Ensuring equal access to public space for people with disabilities requires detailed, up-to-date information on urban accessibility. Historically, such data was fragmented, outdated or manually collected.

name: Using smart algorithms to map whether building or demolishing certain homes improves liveability
desc: The Municipality of Breda uses smart algorithms to investigate whether building or demolishing certain types of homes improves the quality of life.

name: VIALIS Real-time incident detection
desc: The aim of this project is to prevent traffic problems based on urban traffic data.

name: VITE-A2 Video and Text AI Analysis for Political Debates
desc: Municipal council meetings are essential democratic forums, yet their length and complexity often discourage citizen engagement and limit transparency. In the Netherlands, local governments sought ways to make political debates more accessible to the public.

name: Vegetation detection Friesland - Remote sensing and image recognition to interpret satellite images
desc: The Province of Friesland needed a more efficient and timely way to monitor vegetation on the Dutch Wadden Islands, where traditional field-based registration had been carried out only once every six or twelve years by inspectors travelling to the islands.

name: Veovo BlipTrack Guest Predictability solution in Amsterdam Airport Schiphol
desc: The solution was firstly implemented to provide automatic queue wait time measurements at security processes. With this data on hand, the airport found it was able to quickly and efficiently resolve issues arising from irregularities and disruptions.

name: Viralcom Egg - accidents in the water
desc: A prototype that can detect accidents in the water through Artificial Intelligence and neural networks and communicate to the rescue services. The goal is to be able to detect drownings underwater so that water safety is increased.

name: W(e). Service.Heerlen (WESH)
authority: Municipality of Heerlen, CBS, VNG, CoTown, Heerlen Mijn Stad, Brightlands
desc: App for citizens, aimed at promoting citizen participation in the maintenance of the public environment. The app allows citizens to take on maintenance jobs. Once they have successfully completed this job, they will receive a financial reward that can be used by local SMEs.

name: WIL Leak Current - Discover abuse and improper use of benefits
authority: Municipality of Houten, Ijsselstein, Lopik, Nieuwegein and Vijfheerenland
desc: WIL Lekstroom is a collaboration between the municipality of Houten, Ijsselstein, Lopik, Nieuwegein and Vijfheerenland and uses algorithms to discover abuse and improper use of benefits.

name: Wabo assistant - Automated environmental permits
desc: The municipality of The Hague needed a more efficient way to manage the intake of environmental-permit applications governed by the Environmental Law General Provisions Act, known as Wabo.

name: Water fields - purification system for rainwater
desc: Cities increasingly face pressure to manage water sustainably while reducing reliance on potable water for non-drinking purposes. The City of Breda implemented “water fields”, a nature-based purification system that collects, buffers, and treats rainwater at district level.

name: Water management SR - Predicting of water levels
authority: Hoogheemraadschap de Stichtse Rijnlanden en Tauw en HAL24k
desc: The use case aims at improving how data science is used to solve complex problems at water treatment plants and management of water levels. A live demonstration of our data intelligence platform Dimension showed how real-time sensor data can be used for efficient and proactive maintenance.

name: Xomnia - Law enforcement optimization system
desc: The municipality of Amsterdam needed a better way to coordinate and evaluate law-enforcement activity across a fragmented operational landscape in which relevant information was dispersed across multiple disconnected systems.

name: Xomnia - The Burglary Predictor
desc: Utrecht wanted to strengthen burglary prevention by moving beyond reactive policing and municipal response towards a more anticipatory understanding of where burglary risk was likely to emerge.

name: Z-Inspection – Assessment for Responsible Artificial Intelligence
desc: Governments adopting automated systems face complex ethical, legal, and social considerations that cannot be addressed through technical evaluation alone. The Z-Inspection pilot in the Province of Fryslân addresses the need for holistic assessment methods that support responsible adoption across public administrations.

name: iRN_iColumbo
desc: Police investigations increasingly involve large volumes of online information, making manual monitoring of digital sources time-consuming and inconsistent. iColumbo was developed within the Dutch police’s Internet Research & Investigation Network (iRN) to support systematic online searches for suspicious material.

name: “Top 600” and “Top400” used for automated risk modelling
desc: Amsterdam authorities introduced the Top 600 and later Top 400 programmes to reduce high-impact crime by targeting individuals assessed as posing significant risk.

name: Air-purifying billboard in Skopje
desc: Severe urban air pollution in Skopje has posed persistent public health and environmental challenges, with limited large-scale institutional interventions.

name: North Macedonia’s government launches AI digital assistant
authority: Government of the Republic of North Macedonia
desc: Investors and companies seeking to understand a country’s business environment often need rapid access to clear information on investment conditions, public incentives, and available state support, yet these answers are frequently spread across multiple institutions and documents.

name: AI decision support in medical emergency calls
desc: Emergency Medical Communication Centres in Norway must rapidly identify stroke cases during 113 calls in order to dispatch appropriate ambulances and alert hospital stroke teams, yet symptom descriptions are often inconsistent and assessments depend on dispatcher experience, creating risks of delayed diagnosis and…

name: AI for cancer treatment
desc: Radiotherapy planning requires precise delineation of tumours and surrounding organs at risk, a process that traditionally involves extensive manual work by oncologists.

name: AI for improved diagnostics in endometrial cancer
desc: Accurate diagnosis and personalised treatment of endometrial cancer require deeper integration of imaging, molecular, and clinical information. While medical imaging reveals structural and functional patterns associated with disease progression, these biomarkers are not yet fully embedded in clinical decision-making.

name: AI for improvement of AID systems
desc: Norwegian highway tunnels rely on Automatic Incident Detection (AID) systems to alert control centres to dangerous events, yet approximately 90 % of alerts are false positives due to misinterpretation of visual changes such as shadows or lighting variations.

name: AI in image-guided neurosurgery
desc: Brain tumour treatment requires careful consideration of tumour characteristics, progression, and response to therapy, yet predicting outcomes remains complex. Clinicians must interpret large volumes of imaging and clinical data to guide personalised treatment decisions.

name: AI to detect incorrect health reimbursement payments
desc: Public health reimbursement systems must balance timely payments with robust controls to prevent incorrect or fraudulent claims. In Norway, Helfo initiated a collaborative innovation project to improve the accuracy of health reimbursement payments and ensure responsible use of public funds.

name: AI-Mind
desc: Dementia places a growing burden on healthcare systems, and early identification of individuals at risk remains a critical unmet need. The AI-Mind project addresses this challenge by focusing on patients with mild cognitive impairment, a group in which approximately half may progress to dementia.

name: AVENUE – Mobility Pilot Project in Stavanger
desc: Designing shared mobility policies that effectively contribute to greenhouse gas reduction is a growing challenge for medium-sized European cities. In Stavanger, authorities require robust evidence to understand how regulatory choices affect travel behaviour and emissions.

name: Ada-bot helps process applications for family reunification
desc: The Norwegian Directorate of Immigration introduced the automated system “Ada” to improve efficiency in processing family reunification applications, which involve high case volumes and legally structured eligibility criteria.

name: AdaptAl - Adaptive control of aluminium production
desc: Aluminium production involves complex, tightly coupled processes that are sensitive to raw material quality, chemical variations, and operational disturbances. Without adaptive control, these variations can exceed tolerance limits, leading to increased costs, waste, and quality issues.

name: Anna, a bot for processing Expense Claim
authority: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
desc: The Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) and Visma has agreed to test letting a bot automatically process expense claims. The university is the first organisation to implement this functionality, financed by the NTNU digitalisation program. The functionality is not available anymore.

name: Automated Measurement of Proliferation in Breast Cancer
desc: Accurate assessment of tumour proliferation is critical for prognosis and treatment decisions in breast cancer, yet current methods are either subjective or labour-intensive.

name: Automated Quantitative Analysis of Endometrioid Intraepithelial Neoplasia (EIN)
desc: Endometrioid intraepithelial neoplasia is a premalignant condition with a significant risk of progression to endometrial cancer, making accurate diagnosis and risk stratification increasingly important.

name: Automated case management of family immigration with a professional background
desc: Norway’s Directorate of Immigration (UDI) faced growing backlogs in citizenship and family immigration applications, driven by rising volumes and fully manual case handling. Processing times regularly exceeded one year, placing strain on applicants, caseworkers and administrative resources.

name: Automated disbursement of the Covid-19 Business Compensation in Norway
authority: Brønnøysund Register Centre under the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries
desc: The digital compensation scheme was created to support Norwegian businesses to endure the financial consequences of the Covid-19 pandemic. The scheme designed was quick, efficient, and can be relaunched when needed.

name: Automated evaluations of applications at NAV
desc: NAV processes a very large number of benefit applications each year, and manual handling of all cases can lead to delays and inconsistent outcomes. This use case addresses the need to improve efficiency while ensuring decisions comply with legislation.

name: Automatic Classification of Skin Lesions in Digital Pathology
desc: The incidence of malignant melanoma has risen sharply in recent decades, placing growing pressure on pathology departments to examine increasing numbers of skin biopsies with limited specialist resources.

name: Automatic posting of invoices - Robot to propose the correct posting
authority: Norwegian Government Agency for Financial Management
desc: Customers of the Norwegian Government Agency for Financial Management spend significant time deciding how incoming invoices should be posted correctly, and uncertainty in this process can lead to late payment, interest charges and unnecessary administrative cost.

name: Automatisert saksbehandling med arkivmessige hensyn for kunstig intelligens
desc: The Norwegian Maritime Authority seeks to modernise certificate issuance and case processing through automation while ensuring proper archival compliance and long-term document preservation. Manual case handling can be resource-intensive and prone to inconsistencies in documentation management.

name: CONWIND: Forskning på smarte driftskontrollteknologier for havvindparker
desc: Offshore wind energy has significant potential but faces operational challenges that limit efficiency and profitability. Larger turbines reduce costs per unit of energy, yet they also create complex wake effects and turbulent wind fields that increase mechanical stress and reduce energy output.

name: Chatbot Frida
desc: NAV introduced Chatbot Frida to improve responsiveness to citizen enquiries and reduce pressure on call centres and service desks. The objective was to provide continuous digital assistance for frequently asked questions related to welfare benefits, employment services and administrative procedures.

name: ClinCode: Computerised clinical ICD-10 coding
desc: Accurate ICD-10 coding is essential for clinical documentation, billing, and healthcare planning, yet the complexity of the coding system often leads to incomplete or incorrect entries. Clinicians face time constraints and administrative burden, which can compromise coding quality.

name: CoSeM - Computational sepsis mining and modelling
desc: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition requiring rapid detection and intervention, yet early signs are often subtle and distributed across unstructured clinical notes and structured patient data. Clinicians face challenges in continuously monitoring complex patient trajectories in real time.

name: DestinE Digital Twin Engine (DTE) workflow for weather forecasting.
desc: Weather forecasting increasingly requires methods that can quantify uncertainty, generate realistic scenario ensembles, and improve temporal detail without unsustainable computational cost.

name: FLAIT – AI-Assisted Airport Safety Reporting through Human–AI Teaming
desc: Airport aprons are complex, high-risk environments where aircraft, vehicles, and personnel operate in close proximity, leading to frequent safety incidents and costly damage. Despite the scale of the risk, safety reporting in many airports remains manual, time-consuming, and prone to underreporting.

name: Fraxinus - An open source, software only, navigation system for bronchoscopy
desc: Bronchoscopy is a critical procedure for diagnosing lung cancer, yet navigating the complex airway structure to reach small peripheral lesions remains challenging.

name: HAL - classification of documents
desc: In a pilot project between 2017 and 2018, the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) applied machine learning and NLP to analyse and classify up to 6,000 annual reports from embassies and delegations, manking it easier to retrieve relevant information, extract key insights, and generate summaries.

name: Heart failure risk prediction by Ahus
desc: Heart failure remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality, often diagnosed at a late stage when intervention options are limited. Akershus University Hospital (Ahus) aims to improve early detection by developing predictive tools that assist clinicians in identifying patients at elevated risk.

name: IARI - AI-based image recognition for railway infrastructure inspection
desc: Ensuring the safety and reliability of railway infrastructure requires frequent inspections of tracks, overhead lines, and supporting structures. Traditional manual inspections are labour-intensive, costly, and often require track closures, disrupting services and limiting inspection frequency.

name: IDDEAS - Individual Digital Decision Assist System for Child and Adolescent Mental Health
desc: Children and adolescents with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder represent a significant proportion of mental health cases in Norway, with long-term consequences if diagnosis and treatment are delayed or inadequate.

name: IM-PACT - Identification of multimorbid patients with modifiable risk profiles using artificial intelligence
desc: Patients with multiple chronic conditions often experience fragmented care, delayed interventions, and limited involvement in decision-making, leading to poorer outcomes and inefficient use of health resources.

name: KartAi - Automate and streamline case management in construction cases
desc: Accurate and up-to-date property and land-use data are essential for urban planning, construction permitting, and public administration. Manual processing of construction cases and maintenance of cadastral and mapping databases is time-consuming and prone to inconsistencies.

name: Ki-67 in neuroendocrine tumours of the gastrointestinal tract
desc: Ki-67 is a critical biomarker for grading and treatment planning in neuroendocrine tumours of the gastrointestinal tract, yet accurate assessment requires counting a large number of cells, making manual evaluation impractical in routine settings.

name: Lånekassen - Improve control on students with loan payments and identification
desc: Lånekassen, the Norwegian State Educational Loan Fund, sought to improve how it selected student cases for account controls related to housing declarations used in grant eligibility.

name: MIM - Machine learning in the Mammography programme
desc: Breast cancer screening programmes generate very large volumes of mammograms, the majority of which show no signs of disease, yet all images must be carefully reviewed by specialists. This creates significant workload pressure and limits the capacity of screening services.

name: MyMDT - My Medical Digital Twin
authority: Norwegian University of Science and Technology
desc: MyMDT – My Medical Digital Twin is a platform designed for personalised management of hypertension, combining physiological simulation, machine learning, and data from wearable devices.

name: NVE Copernicus 2
authority: Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate
desc: Norway faces significant risks from floods and avalanches, requiring timely monitoring of snow and water conditions. The Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE), in collaboration with Norsk Regnesentral, aims to enhance emergency warning systems by improving environmental data analysis.

name: Nancy - Access to National library assets
desc: The Norwegian National Library needed a more effective way to open up its extensive collections of text, images and video so that users could discover, search and understand cultural assets more deeply.

name: Naturinngrep i inngrepsfri natur
desc: The Norwegian Environment Agency is responsible for maintaining a national map of intervention-free nature, defined as areas located at least one kilometre from the nearest technical infrastructure or human intervention.

name: NewbornTime
desc: Accurate documentation of events during newborn resuscitation and early care is essential for clinical quality, training, and patient safety, yet manual recording is often incomplete or imprecise.

name: NorGPT - The open LLM "Made in Norway"
desc: NorGPT is a Large Language Model using Norwegian Language developed by NorwAI and the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) to allow users work on language-related tasks more effectively instead of learning an artificial syntax, so that they can formulate their queries in natural language.

name: Norsk Hydro's AI tool to detect hackers
desc: Large industrial operators face significant risks from cyberattacks targeting operational technology and production infrastructure, as demonstrated by the 2019 ransomware attack against Norsk Hydro.

name: Norway AI for Diagnosing and treating Breast cancer
desc: Norwegian researchers are addressing a critical clinical challenge in breast-cancer care: how to improve the accuracy of diagnosis and treatment selection by making better use of the country’s extensive, well-structured healthcare data.

name: Norway Chatbots Kommune Kiri - Chatbot for public administrations
desc: Norwegian government agencies and municipalities have increasingly adopted chatbots to improve how citizens access public services and information.

name: Norwegian Tax Administration chat service
desc: The Norwegian Tax Administration introduced its chat service to address a familiar public-service challenge: large numbers of taxpayers need timely answers to general questions, particularly when they are trying to understand obligations, complete filings correctly or resolve routine issues without delay.

name: Norwegian University of Science and Technology testing the utility and safety of Microsoft's AI assistant in public sector organisations
authority: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
desc: Public sector organisations increasingly explore productivity assistants but lack clear guidance on organisational readiness, data protection and responsible deployment. In Norway, public institutions sought evidence-based insights before large-scale adoption.

name: Optical Character Recognition (OCR)
desc: The National Archives of Norway sought to enhance access to digitised historical documents by automating transcription and metadata extraction processes. Large volumes of scanned archival material required efficient processing to enable searchability and identification of sensitive content.

name: PHM Hydro – Performance and Health Monitoring for Hydropower Plants
authority: Royal Norwegian Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries
desc: Hydropower operators depend on the reliable performance of turbines, generators, and auxiliary equipment to ensure safe, continuous, and profitable electricity production. Unplanned downtime or undetected efficiency losses can lead to significant economic impacts and operational risks.

name: Pathology services in the Western Norway Health Region – a center for applied digitization: Optimization of the pathology workflow
desc: Pathology departments face growing workloads due to increasing sample volumes and analytical complexity, while staffing levels remain relatively stable. Inefficient workflows risk longer turnaround times and increased strain on personnel.

name: Personalised decision support for patients with chronic pain
desc: Chronic pain affects a diverse patient population with varying causes, responses to treatment, and side effects, making it difficult to identify optimal therapies. Existing decision support tools are largely generic and fail to account for individual patient differences.

name: Phenotyping for Genetic Analysis Requisitioning
desc: Accurate requisitioning of genetic tests for hereditary conditions depends on clear and structured descriptions of patient phenotypes, yet clinicians often document symptoms in free text, making the process time-consuming and error-prone.

name: Predicting sick leave duration
desc: The Norwegian Labour and Welfare Service needed a more structured way to support case workers dealing with people on sick leave, particularly when deciding which cases require closer follow-up and which may need less attention.

name: Predicting the risk of postoperative wound infections with AI
desc: The main goal is to develop an AI-based tool that can indicate the probability of a postoperative wound infection occurring in the individual patient, so that risk-reducing measures can be taken and the burden of disease for the patient is reduced.

name: Prediction of relapse in glioblastoma
desc: Glioblastoma is an aggressive brain tumour with a poor prognosis, and recurrence after surgery is common, often occurring in tissue surrounding the original tumour site.

name: RE-SIKTET- Conversation and documentation quality in medical telephone assessment assisted by artificial intelligence
desc: Emergency medical call centres play a critical role in patient safety, yet telephone assessments are complex, time-pressured, and highly dependent on operator experience. Important questions may be missed, documentation quality can vary, and subtle indicators of serious conditions may be overlooked.

name: Research grant for case management AI

name: La Paula i la Rita - the chatbot assistants in the authentication processes in Catalunya
authority: AOC Consorci Administració Oberta de Catalunya
desc: Catalonia's Open Administration Consortium (AOC) receives over 91,000 annual support requests, with citizens struggling to navigate complex e-government procedures for digital identification and certificate management.

name: Leveraging Large Language Models for Topic Classification in the Domain of Public Affair
authority: BiDA - Lab, Universidad Autónoma de Madrid (UAM)
desc: Public affairs documents shape regulation, compliance and democratic oversight, yet their volume and complexity make systematic analysis challenging for both public institutions and private organisations. This research pilot investigates how large language models can support the classification of public affairs texts.

name: Local.iA: promoting public and responsible AI
desc: Local.iA is an ecosystem of resources, materials, and initiatives that provides local authorities—free of charge—with training paths, guides, and communication materials to deploy AI and data governance in an organised manner.

name: Madrid - AI for saving lives of Psychiatric patients
desc: This use case focused on supporting clinicians in identifying suicide risk and other serious health threats among psychiatric patients more rapidly and consistently.

name: Madrid Mobility 360 (multimodal planner for urban commuting)
authority: Empresa Municipal de Transported del Ayuntamiento de Madrid
desc: Madrid Mobility 360 was developed to provide residents and visitors with an integrated digital tool for planning journeys across multiple transport modes in the city. Urban commuters often face fragmented information across public transport, carsharing and bicycle services.

name: MasterMind - Basque Country
authority: Osakidetza (Servicio Vasco de Salud/Basque Health System)
desc: The objective of the MasterMind project was “to make high quality treatment for depression more widely available for adults suffering from the illness by the use of ICT” (http://mastermind-project.eu). Collaboration by 23 partners framed in a European H2020 project was created in order to accomplish this objective.

name: Mercé - citizen science for better urban life
desc: The Mercè project in Barcelona was a citizen science experiment run in 2020 where residents helped train algorithms to make cities more livable.

name: Misty II - Robot for elderly people
desc: This use case was designed to explore whether a social robot could improve the daily lives of older people living alone by providing practical support, companionship and routine assistance in the home.

name: Multiple chatbots on the spanish Agenzia Tributaria website
desc: In this section users can find a whole set of virtual assistance tools for Personal Income Tax, Censuses, VAT, SII and Collection, made up of virtual assistants, Informants, Income Tax and Censuses, search engines for economic activities, Locators of operations for the delivery of goods and provision of services.

name: OLI Chatbot across spanish airports
desc: Airports manage complex passenger flows and high volumes of enquiries related to flights, terminals, and services, particularly during peak travel periods. AENA, the operator of Spanish airports, introduced OLI to improve passenger experience and reduce pressure on staff.

name: Open Spanish LLM model in collaboration with IBM
desc: IBM and the Spanish government are collaborating to create an open-source large language model focused on Spanish. The project aims to provide advanced generative AI tools for nearly 500 million Spanish speakers worldwide. It will also support other Iberian languages like Catalan, Basque, and Galician.

name: Optimize risk prediction after myocardial infarction through artificial intelligence and multidimensional evaluation
authority: Fundacion para la Investigacion de Malaga en Biomedicina y salud
desc: Accurate risk prediction following myocardial infarction is essential to guide treatment decisions and prevent adverse outcomes, yet existing models rely on limited clinical variables. This project seeks to enhance postoperative risk stratification by integrating multidimensional patient data.

name: PALOMA - Madrid’s AI-powered virtual assistant
desc: Unwanted loneliness among elderly people is a growing social challenge with significant health and wellbeing implications. The City of Madrid introduced PALOMA to proactively identify and support older residents at risk of social isolation.

name: PREDUCA - Student learning pathways personalisation
desc: Public education systems must address diverse student needs while planning resources efficiently at scale. The Andalusian Government developed PREDUCA to personalise learning pathways and support strategic planning in public education.

name: ParticipApp - more inclusive, transparent, and effective citizen participation in government decision-making
authority: Ministry for Digital Transformation and the Civil Service
desc: ParticipApp is a national digital platform designed to make citizen participation in government decision-making more inclusive, transparent, and effective. The platform allows contributions in all co-official languages of Spain, and supports multiple input types, including text, voice, and images of handwritten notes.

name: Pred Crime Pilot Rivas-Vaciamadrid
desc: In 2016, the local police of Rivas-Vaciamadrid, a town of 86,000 people in the Madrid region, ran a pilot of the Pred-Crime software, developed by Spanish company EuroCop (Europa Press, 2015).

name: Proactive administrative procedures
desc: Public administrations often place a heavy administrative burden on citizens, requiring repeated data entry and proactive applications for benefits, which disadvantages those with limited bureaucratic capacity.

name: Process Mining pilot for the support service and case management of the Diputació de Girona
desc: Public sector support and case management services often appear straightforward but can hide significant operational complexity that affects efficiency, response times, and resource allocation.

name: Provincia IA –  AI pilot projects in key public services in the Province of Castellón
desc: The Castellón Provincial Council, consistently attuned to emerging challenges, seeks to position itself as a leader in shaping the legal, technological, and social framework that will support the responsible and orderly use of artificial intelligence as a driver of modernisation across the entire province.

name: REACHOUT: Smart Cities: from smart waste to smart tourism
authority: Logroño municipality and the La Rioja and Cantabria regional governments
desc: As cities aim to start using big data and automated processes to become “smart”, a series of ADM systems have been embedded at the municipal level in Spain. These systems usually support decision-making rather than working entirely autonomously.

name: RadioVal - International Clinical Validation of Radiomics Artificial Intelligence for Breast Cancer Treatment Planning
desc: Radiomics has the potential to support more personalised cancer treatment, but its clinical adoption is limited by the lack of large-scale validation, consistency across centres, and evidence of real-world usability.

name: Recognition of university degrees with AI
authority: Ministry of Science, Innovation, and Universities
desc: Lengthy recognition processes for foreign university degrees have historically delayed labour market integration for qualified professionals in Spain. The Ministry of Science, Innovation, and Universities sought to modernise this process to address skills shortages and administrative inefficiencies.

name: Robic: Inclusive AI for Special Learning
desc: This pilot project explores the feasibility and educational impact of an AI-supported social robotics solution in a special education setting.

name: Robotic Automation Plan
desc: The Robot Automation Plan has created a new service for robotic process automation.

name: Robotic System Da Vinci
desc: Hospitals and surgical teams continually seek ways to perform delicate and complex operations with greater precision, less trauma to the patient and shorter recovery times, particularly in procedures where conventional open surgery may involve larger incisions and longer rehabilitation.

name: Robots - Automating Covid-19 tests
desc: During the COVID-19 emergency, Spanish authorities faced the urgent challenge of scaling up testing capacity quickly enough to support public-health management and identify infections at a much larger volume than manual processes could comfortably handle.

name: SAFELIGHT project: Analysis of visibility in roads and streets during the night to avoid accidents of vulnerable users
authority: Municipality of Las Rozas de Madrid
desc: Many urban locations, such as pedestrian crossings, cycle lanes and narrow pavements near traffic, become especially hazardous at night when poor visibility increases the risk of accidents for vulnerable road users.

name: SAMPA - Service of registration and promotion of the adherence to medications in elderly patients
desc: Medication non-adherence among elderly and chronic patients leads to poorer health outcomes and higher healthcare costs. At the University Hospital Miguel Servet (HUMS) in Zaragoza, outpatient pharmacy processes were fragmented, manual, and prone to dispensing and coordination errors.

name: SIMPATICO Platform for PS iN Spain
desc: The SIMPATICO Platform was developed to simplify how citizens and companies interact with public services by improving the usability and relevance of digital administrative systems.

name: SMARTECOMOUNTAINS Project in Andalusia
desc: The SMARTECOMOUNTAINS project, led by the University of Granada within the LifeWatch ERIC research infrastructure, develops advanced digital tools to study biodiversity and global change in mountain ecosystems.

name: Scaviho: scalable vegetation index and harvesting forecaster
desc: Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) is widely used in precision agriculture due to versatility and reliability in reporting general crop’s canopy status and is used during all the season.

name: Sentilo BCN - Plataforma de Sensors i Actuadors de Barcelona
desc: The Barcelona City Council, through the Municipal Institute of Informatics (IMI), started in November 2012 a project conceived for define the strategy and the necessary actions in order to achieve global positioning Barcelona as a reference in the field of Smart Cities.

name: Smart lighting with AI in Barcelona
desc: Urban congestion contributes significantly to travel delays, emissions and reduced quality of life in large cities. In Barcelona, traffic management required more adaptive solutions to respond to real-time conditions.

name: Spain’s Social Security administration: Using AI to deliver benefits to citizens more efficiently with the ISSA Social Security Virtual Assistant
desc: Spain’s Social Security administration handles millions of citizen enquiries each year, creating heavy workloads and long waiting times for routine information requests. To improve service delivery, the administration introduced a virtual assistant to provide immediate access to official guidance.

name: Speeding up judicial proceedings with Transkit, an AI-based tool that transcribes trials
desc: Legal proceedings have a peculiarity when it comes to the drafting of judgments. Sometimes the transcriptions of the meetings are needed, especially when the judgment is escalated to higher instances.

name: Streamlining administrative tasks through robotic process automation in the administration of Justice
authority: Ministerio de la Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes
desc: Justice administrations handle large volumes of repetitive administrative tasks that contribute to delays in legal procedures and increased workload for staff. In Spain, backlogs in processes such as nationality applications and criminal record cancellations highlighted the need for operational efficiency improvements.

name: Streamlining talent acquisition and verification with RPA (Robotic Process Automation)
desc: Public-sector recruitment processes often require extensive manual verification of candidates’ qualifications, creating delays and heavy workloads. The Andalusian Health Service introduced robotic process automation to streamline verification of certificates and documents submitted during selection processes.

name: Tool to optimise self-consumption in residential sectors
desc: Households and residential communities increasingly want to make better use of locally generated renewable electricity, but optimising self-consumption is difficult because it depends on understanding both generation patterns and highly variable consumption behaviour.

name: Track AI
desc: The objective of the Track AI project is to incorporate artificial intelligence (AI) into the DIVE medical device so it can “estimate the probability of the patient having a certain pathology”. The innovation was created due to the difficulty in exploring the visual function (e.g.

name: Usage of Generative Ai in Spain justice
desc: Judicial systems face growing workloads, complex legal texts and increasing expectations for timely communication with citizens. In Spain, pilot initiatives have explored how generative language technologies can support judicial professionals without compromising legal safeguards.

name: Using Artificial Intelligence to detect and predict river overflows
authority: Centre de Telecomunicacions i Tecnologies de la Informació de la Generalitat de Catalunya (CTTI)
desc: Flood risk management requires rapid and accurate assessment of potential river overflows, yet traditional hydraulic models can be computationally intensive and slow to update.

name: VI-DAS – Vision Inspired Driver Assistance Systems
desc: VI-DAS addressed the need for safer, more adaptive driver-assistance systems by focusing on contextual understanding of driver behaviour and road situations using non-invasive sensing.

name: Valencia Provincial Council – Gestri Tax Enquiries Chatbot
desc: Rental subsidy programmes are critical social policies but are often slowed by manual document verification and repeated requests for information. The Valencian Regional Government developed a digital solution to streamline these procedures.

name: Valencia shows how integrated geospatial systems can be used to build AI-empowered cities
desc: Valencia used geospatial technologies, drones and AI‑driven spatial analysis to support emergency response during and after the October 2024 DANA floods, one of the most severe flood events in recent local history.

name: VeriPol - Detect false police reports
desc: False police reports, especially for low-level offences, consume investigative resources, distort crime recording and can be linked to wider fraudulent behaviour, making them a costly problem for law-enforcement agencies.

name: VicomTTS - Quality synthetic voices
desc: VicomTTS was developed to address the limited availability of high-quality digital services in the Basque language, which can hinder its everyday use in public, educational and personal contexts.

name: VioGen - Forecast gender violence
desc: Spain introduced VioGen to support one of the most sensitive and high-stakes areas of public protection: assessing the risk faced by victims of gender-based violence and determining the level of police protection required.

name: VisitMadridGPT - Transforming tourism in Madrid
desc: Tourists visiting Madrid require timely, accurate, and personalised information to navigate attractions, transport, and services, while the city seeks better insight into visitor needs. VisitMadridGPT addresses both challenges by enhancing digital tourism services.

name: Water Management with AI in Seville
authority: EMPRESA METROPOLITANA DE ABASTECIMIENTO Y SANEAMIENTO DE AGUAS DE SEVILLA, S.A. (EMASESA)
desc: Managing the integral water cycle in large urban areas involves monitoring consumption, distribution networks and environmental conditions across diverse data sources. Fragmented systems can limit predictive capabilities and operational efficiency.

name: WellCo - Wellbeing and health virtual coach
authority: HI IBERIA INGENIERIA Y PROYECTOS SL and Fondazione Bruno Kessler
desc: Supporting citizens in maintaining long-term physical, cognitive, mental, and social wellbeing is a growing societal challenge, particularly in ageing populations where lifestyle-related risks accumulate over time.

name: ZEBAI - Innovative methodologies for the design of Zero-Emission and cost-effective Buildings enhanced by Artificial Intelligence
desc: The construction sector faces growing pressure to reduce emissions while maintaining affordability and high indoor environmental quality. ZEBAI aims to develop innovative methodologies for designing zero-emission and cost-effective buildings through a holistic, data-driven approach.

name: iMaging Project - Beach Monitoring
authority: SOCIB - Balearic Islands Ocean Observing and Forecasting System
desc: Coastal authorities need timely and reliable information on beach conditions in order to protect the public, monitor environmental health and respond quickly to changing marine dynamics.

name: AI Safety Perception Patterns
desc: Perceived safety is a critical factor influencing how citizens use and experience urban spaces, yet it is difficult to measure systematically over time.

name: AI4EU-TAILOR
desc: Foundations of Trustworthy AI - Integrating Reasoning, Learning and Optimization.

name: AIDA - Interpreting detailed plan provisions
desc: Sweden’s planning system has long relied on a large stock of existing detailed plans that must be digitised before they can be integrated into a coherent national plan database.

name: ARTIMATION Project: Building trust in air traffic management AI
desc: The ARTIMATION project, funded under the SESAR Joint Undertaking, addresses the challenge of transparency in artificial intelligence systems used in air traffic management (ATM). Increasing reliance on automation and predictive models in ATM requires high levels of trust, safety and regulatory compliance.

name: Artificial intelligence finds disease-related genes
desc: An artificial neural network can reveal patterns in huge amounts of gene expression data, and discover groups of disease-related genes. This has been shown by a new study led by researchers at Linköping University, published in Nature Communications.

name: Automated processes Uddevalla - AI to internal processes
desc: Uddevalla municipality has 10 automated processes underway, which corresponds to 20 full-time positions' annual work. Until 2021, more automated processes will be started, which will free up twice as many full-time jobs.

name: Borås Municipality assesses AI chatbot improvements to customer service during pilot
desc: Borås Municipality faces a high volume of routine enquiries from residents seeking information on municipal services, which can place pressure on customer service teams and slow response times.

name: Chatbot Skatti - Swedish Tax Agency
desc: The Swedish Tax Agency introduced Chatbot Skatti to provide accessible guidance on tax-related matters through its official website. Citizens frequently seek clarification on filing procedures, deadlines, deductions and digital services, creating recurring enquiries.

name: Checks for financial support - AI for checking companies requesting support
desc: The Public Employment Services is actively working and experimenting with AI. ADM is used to perform financial checks on companies seeking financial support to help them employ the long-term unemployed.

name: Detection causes early school leavers Kungsbacka - Analysing data of early school leavers
desc: Each year in Kungsbacka, around 100 students move from primary school to upper secondary education without the eligibility required to continue successfully, creating a significant concern for educators and local authorities.

name: EXTRA-BRAIN - Explainable Trustworthy brain-like AI for Data Intensive Applications
desc: Data-intensive applications increasingly require learning systems that are energy-efficient, adaptable across tasks, and transparent to users, particularly when deployed across edge and cloud environments.

name: Event Impact Calculator in Gothenburg
desc: Cities and event organisers need reliable tools to assess the economic, environmental, and social impacts of events, yet such analysis is often complex and costly. Gothenburg developed the Event Impact Calculator to support sustainable event planning.

name: FARMWISE - Future Agricultural Resource Management and Water Innovations for a Sustainable Europe
desc: European agriculture faces mounting pressure to optimise water use, increase productivity and reduce environmental impact under climate variability. FARMWISE aims to support farmers and decision-makers with an advanced decision-support system that enhances resource management and sustainable practices.

name: Financial Assistance Automation
desc: Nacka wants to be a modern municipality where the administrators will have more time for individual support with a focus on self-sufficiency through reduced administration. In 2017, work was therefore started on introducing e-service and in December of the same year, the processing process was automated.

name: Forecasting Sweeish GDP with Explainable AI
desc: The innovation project at the Swedish National Financial Management Authority (ESV) was set out to find a solution to these needs of Explainable AI (XML) as well as building grounds for integrating AI in the financial management of Swedish government.

name: GPT-SW3 - The first large-scale generative language model for the Swedish language
desc: Swedish organisations increasingly need language technologies that reflect local linguistic realities and can be developed within a national ecosystem rather than relying entirely on foreign models.

name: Kari - Chatbot for local governments
desc: Kari was created to help local municipalities manage large volumes of citizen enquiries about public services in a faster and more consistent way.

name: Kommers (KAI) semantics check tool
desc: Public procurement processes in both public and private sector organisations require clear, unambiguous tender documentation to ensure fair competition and avoid misinterpretation by potential bidders.

name: LAIban - A chatbot for children
desc: Children in municipal preschools frequently ask practical questions about daily routines, activities and schedules, which can place additional demands on staff. The City of Helsingborg introduced LAIban to support children’s independence while complementing the role of educators.

name: MIMER New AI-optimised Supercomputer
desc: Mimer is Sweden’s AI Innovation Factory, designed to accelerate AI adoption for industry and research. It provides access to high-performance GPU infrastructure and a team of AI specialists to support companies, startups, and researchers in developing, deploying, and scaling AI solutions.

name: Natural language processing for Land Registry documentation in Sweden
desc: The handwritten documents were of low quality and resolution which made analysis challenging. To fix this, the SLR carried out pre-processing work on the handwritten documents to improve the quality of the input data.

name: Planning for flexible manufacturing with robots
desc: Planning techniques are used in conjunction with scheduling techniques to automate the process of making front axles for heavy vehicle applications. The solution will first require extracting expert knowledge from the human planners and formalizing it in a way that can be used in automated planning.

name: RPA in Södertälje - Automation of internal services
desc: The Municipality of Södertälje faced inefficiencies and administrative bottlenecks in handling routine internal services such as absence reporting for hourly employees, termination of hourly contracts, travel service bookings and the issuance of employer certificates.

name: SCAPIS - Prevention of heart- and lung-diseases
authority: Uppsala, Umeå, Linköping, Malmö/Lund, Gothenburg and Stockholm Hospitals
desc: SCAPIS was established to strengthen prevention and risk assessment for cardiovascular and pulmonary diseases through a large-scale population study capable of generating deeper insight into how these conditions develop and how they might be prevented or delayed.

name: SKOSA - Interpreting medical information
desc: Administrators handling health-related casework often need to review large volumes of medical information and translate complex clinical material into structured assessments that support benefit or needs-related decisions.

name: Self-driving buses roll into Gothenburg
desc: Cities seeking to modernise public transport must balance sustainability goals, service accessibility, and the safe introduction of new mobility technologies.

name: Stockholm3 - Diagnosing prostate cancer with OncoWatch
desc: This use case focuses on improving the diagnosis of prostate cancer by strengthening the consistency, accuracy and scalability of pathology assessment across laboratories and clinical settings. Diagnosing prostate cancer can be complex, and variability in interpretation may affect both efficiency and quality of care.

name: Svea - A shared digital assistant for the public sector
authority: Kungsbacka municipality, Tjörn municipality, Gothenburg city, Region Skåne, Region Halland, and Västra Götaland Region
desc: Public-sector organisations handle large volumes of text-based work every day, from drafting and revising documents to summarising material, classifying content, and supporting administrative processes, yet these tasks consume significant staff time and are difficult for single organisations to automate alone.

name: Swedish municipality deploys robots for safer recruitment
desc: Upplands-Bro Municipality uses the Tengai AI interview system to conduct structured, resume-free candidate screenings. The tool asks all applicants identical questions to minimise unconscious bias and focus on skills.

name: Swedish police used face recognition until 2019 at the Skavsta airport
desc: As part of Operation Rimfrost, aimed at combating organised crime, the Swedish Police tested facial recognition tools to identify suspects across images from crime scenes and CCTV footage. The objective was to enhance investigative capabilities by quickly identifying recurring individuals across large image datasets.

name: Tengai - Robot in recruitment processes
desc: Upplands-Bro Municipality began using Tengai in June 2019 to address a persistent challenge in recruitment: reducing bias in candidate selection while maintaining a structured and efficient hiring process.

name: Vaxjo Kommun chatbot
desc: The Växjö Municipality website includes a chatbot that assists residents and visitors with general inquiries. It helps users quickly access information about municipal services, local regulations, community resources, and ongoing initiatives, improving accessibility and easing navigation across the site.

name: ViEWS - The Political Violence Early-Warning System
desc: The Violence Early-Warning System was launched in 2017 by Uppsala University and the Peace Research Institute Oslo to support policymakers and humanitarian actors in anticipating organised political violence.

name: WISDOM - Well-being improvement through the Integration of healthcare and reSearch Data and models with Out border for chronic iMmune-mediated diseases
desc: Chronic immune-mediated diseases affect around 10 % of Europeans and require coordinated, data-driven approaches to improve outcomes. However, fragmentation of medical and research data limits comprehensive analysis and personalised care strategies.

name: Yasmine - Robot employee
desc: Nacka municipality is part of Stockholm county, and it has developed and implemented a so-called robot employee called Yasmine. The robot is part of an RPA service platform that was provided by the Norwegian company Basefarm. So far, the administration of Nacka has automated three processes.

name: AI tool to predict recidivism in prisoners in Switzerland
authority: Swiss Execution of Penal Sentences and Justice
desc: Swiss penal authorities implemented the Risk-Oriented Sanctioning framework to structure sentence execution and reduce reoffending through systematic case management. The framework divides offender management into triage, assessment, planning and progress stages.

name: Chatbot - Offer residents and tourism information and services from the administration
desc: The City of St. Gallen tested this chatbot to improve how residents and tourists access municipal information and services, particularly in situations where users need quick, practical answers without navigating multiple systems.

name: Chatbot - Security institution information, find the ones entitled to premium reductions
desc: In the Canton of St. Gallen, the social security institution needed a more accessible way to provide citizens with information about its services, particularly where people may be unsure about entitlements or may not know how to navigate the institution’s offerings.

name: Fall-Screening-Tool FaST - Assisting risk-oriented sanctioning
authority: Swiss Execution of Penal Sentences and Justice
desc: The Swiss Execution of Penal Sentences and Justice has been introducing a tool called Fall-Screening-Tool to assist in the classification of cases in Risk-Oriented Sanctioning.

name: LoRaWAN - The IoT network for Zurich
authority: EWZ -  Service Division of the Department of Public Utilities and Transport of the City of Zurich
