desc: EWZ has built up a comprehensive Long Ranage IoT network in Zurich. It uses the freely available LoRaWAN (long-range wide-area network) industry standard, which enables incredibly simple and cost-effective data transmission.

name: MPAI Community: Moving Picture, Audio and Data Coding by Artificial Intelligence (MPAI)
desc: Moving Picture, Audio and Data Coding by Artificial Intelligence (MPAI) is an international, unaffiliated, non-profit organisation with the mission is to develop Artificial Intelligence (AI) enabled data coding specifications, with clear Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) licensing frameworks, of Moving Picture, Audio…

name: Machine Learning SoSi (ML_SoSi)
desc: Grouping of typical prospective progression patterns with regard to benefit payments in the system of social security and gainful employment as well as estimation of group membership by using individual characteristics and retrospective progression data using a machine learning approach.

name: Mapping Vulnerable Populations with AI
desc: Policymakers require accurate, up-to-date insights into the spatial distribution of vulnerable populations to design targeted social, health and disaster response interventions. Conventional census-based methods may lack timeliness or granularity.

name: Maxi - Chatbot answering questions on insurance
authority: Social Insurance Institute of Canton of Aargau
desc: Social Insurance Aargau introduced the Maxi chatbot to deal with a high volume of routine enquiries and to reduce the operational burden created by daily incoming questions.

name: MedicalGuide project
desc: Canton Aargau has been involved in the MedicalGuide project, which provides users with an initial assessment of disease by using a Chatbot

name: NOGAuto - Assign or control codes to companies for economic activities
desc: The Federal Statistical Office depends on accurate and stable NOGA coding in the Business and Enterprise Register because these economic-activity classifications directly influence the quality of structural, economic and synthetic business statistics.

name: Plausibility check on quality and reliability of administrative data
desc: This use case addresses the substantial effort required by statistical offices to validate the quality and reliability of administrative and survey data before it can be used confidently.

name: Refugees - Assigning asylum seekers
desc: This use case was designed to improve how asylum seekers are assigned to Swiss cantons by replacing purely random allocation with a method intended to increase their chances of labour-market integration.

name: ZüriCityGPT
desc: People seeking information about city administration often face a familiar problem: official websites contain a great deal of useful content, but search and navigation do not always produce direct answers to practical questions.

name: AI4Life - AI-based smart intersection management system in Instanbul
desc: AI4Life in Istanbul addressed congestion, emissions, and safety risks at urban intersections, where inefficient traffic flow contributes significantly to economic and environmental costs.

name: A Sovereign AI Model: National LLM to Enter Beta in 2026
desc: Ukraine is developing its own sovereign large language model (LLM)—a national artificial intelligence system tailored to the Ukrainian language, culture and public-sector needs.

name: AI helps diagnose tuberculosis and other lung pathologies
authority: Public Health Center of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine (PHC)
desc: The project uses artificial intelligence (AI) to assist in diagnosing Tuberculosis (TB) and other lung diseases by analysing chest X‑rays.

name: AI to notify the police about suspicious persons
desc: In Zakarpattia, Ukraine, authorities have started using artificial intelligence to support police monitoring of suspicious activity. Video cameras across the region are connected to an AI system that analyses live footage and identifies people behaving unusually, especially near strategic infrastructure.

name: Brainscan Telemedicine - AI for brain diagnostics
desc: In Odesa, Ukraine, authorities have launched a pilot telemedicine project called BrainScan that uses artificial intelligence to dramatically speed up the diagnosis of brain diseases and injuries — a critical factor when every minute can save a life.

name: Cassandra – Automated risk assessment system used by the Ukraine Ministry of Justice
desc: Judicial systems often seek tools to support consistent and efficient pre-trial and pre-sentence decision-making, particularly in assessing the likelihood of re-offending.

name: CheckEye: The first AI-based platform in Europe implementing a national chronic disease screening
desc: CheckEye is the first AI-based platform in Europe to implement a national screening program for chronic diseases and their complications, first deployed in Ukraine in 2024 across six regions during wartime.

name: Digital Twin for the Reconstruction of Ukraine
desc: The European Union’s Digital Twin for the Reconstruction of Ukraine is an AI‑enabled initiative led by the European AI Office to support Ukraine’s rebuilding efforts.

name: Digital assistant "Mriya" for learning
desc: In 2024, Ukraine’s Ministry of Digital Transformation launched Mriya, a digital assistant specifically designed to support education across the country.

name: Diia.AI: The World's First National AI Agent for Government Services
authority: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
desc: On September 1, 2025, Ukraine became the first country in the world to introduce an AI assistant for government services via its Diia portal. Announced by Digital Transformation Minister Mykhailo Fedorov on Telegram, the AI tool is currently in open beta testing.

name: DoZorro AI tool
desc: The monitoring portal DoZorro is a platform where each participant in the system (supplier, customer, controlling authority, citizen) can provide feedback to the government customer or supplier.

name: ProZorro, Bid prediction
desc: The ProZorro team is using Artificial Intelligence and machine learning in its work with the aim of developing a model that would predict the likelihood of a tender happening and being succesful.

name: ProZorro, CPV Prediction
desc: Prozorro has developed an AI tool that can predict the correct CPV codes and unit of measurement. The tool has not yet been implemented. It aims to make the platforms that provide the user-interface for organisations using the Prozorro data easier to use, reducing mis-classifications and errors.

name: 80 councils in the UK use AI to identify possible frauds in welfare claims
desc: Local authorities in the UK are responsible for administering welfare benefits while preventing fraud and error. To manage limited investigative resources, around 80 councils introduced automated risk screening tools to flag claims for further review.

name: AI Sweeps new govs in UK
desc: Public administrations process large volumes of emails, documents, reports, and routine communications, and this creates pressure to improve productivity without increasing administrative burden.

name: AI camera system catches litter louts in Loughborough
desc: Littering in public spaces imposes environmental, financial and social costs on local authorities and communities. In Loughborough, an intelligent camera system was deployed on Warwick Way to deter and detect individuals discarding waste from vehicles.

name: AI planning for integrated urban traffic control
desc: The advent of Connected Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) presents a unique opportunity for a fundamental change in urban traffic control. CAVs hold the promise of significant benefits in terms of accident prevention, decreased carbon emissions, time savings, and better traffic control.

name: AI traffic system in Pittsburgh
desc: Pittsburgh needed a more effective way to manage congestion caused by a difficult urban road network shaped by hills, bridges and irregular street layouts. Traditional pre-programmed traffic signals were poorly suited to these changing conditions and contributed to delays, excess idling and inefficient traffic flow.

name: AI-controlled Smart Traffic Junctions in Manchester
desc: The rapid growth of walking and cycling requires traffic management systems that can dynamically prioritise different road users while maintaining safety and efficiency. In Greater Manchester, traditional signal control struggled to adapt to changing travel patterns, particularly during increased active travel uptake.

name: Aila: AI Lesson Assistant for UK teachers
authority: Department for Education (DfE) / Oak National Academy
desc: Teachers face significant workload pressures when preparing high-quality, curriculum-aligned lesson plans tailored to diverse student needs. Oak National Academy developed Aila to support teachers in lesson planning while maintaining pedagogical quality and alignment with national curricula.

name: Alexa skill - enquiring about tax credits
desc: HM Revenue and Customs launched an Alexa skill to support over three million tax credit customers during renewal periods, when contact volumes are typically high. The objective was to provide accessible guidance on renewal deadlines, required information and general eligibility queries.

name: Alexa skill - personalised weather report and forecast
desc: The UK Met Office introduced an Alexa “Flash Briefing” skill to provide personalised weather forecasts and updates through voice interaction. The operational goal was to extend access to official meteorological information beyond traditional broadcast and web channels.

name: Alexa skill - vehicle tax and MOT
desc: The Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency introduced an Alexa skill to simplify access to information about vehicle tax and MOT expiry dates. Vehicle owners often needed quick confirmation of compliance deadlines without navigating government websites.

name: Alexa skill and Google home app - checking state pension age
desc: The Department for Work and Pensions developed a prototype voice service enabling citizens to check their state pension age through Amazon Alexa and Google Home devices. Many users sought quick clarification of eligibility timelines without navigating detailed guidance pages.

name: Amelia - Chatbot helping local residents find city services
desc: Local residents often struggle to identify which city service they need, where to find it and how to begin an interaction with the relevant department, particularly when public-service structures are complex and spread across multiple channels.

name: Automated Facial Recognition technology within the UK's South Wales Police Department
desc: Over the course of 2020, the UK witnessed the first high profile application of the Law Enforcement Directive 15 concerning the use of face recognition technologies in public spaces by the police.

name: Automated decision making system to determine the risk represented by visa applicants
desc: In August 2020, the UK government's Home Office abandoned an ADM system called the "Streaming tool" that assessed the risk of visa applicants.

name: Babylon - Health interactive symptom checker
desc: Babylon’s interactive symptom checker was developed to help people obtain timely, structured health information when they were trying to understand possible symptoms and decide what to do next.

name: Barking and Dagenham AI Search and Webchat - Streamlining access to council services and information through AI-powered search and chat
desc: Residents often struggle to navigate council websites or contact centres to find accurate information on local services, leading to high call volumes and repeated enquiries.

name: Behaviour Analytics to Measure Impact of Social Distancing in Transport
desc: During the COVID-19 pandemic, transport authorities faced unprecedented challenges in ensuring passenger safety while maintaining essential mobility services.

name: Birmingham City Council takes aim at illegal dumping with its AI-enabled CCTV camera pilot
desc: Cameras placed near dumping hotspots are trained to identify waste placed anywhere other than public bins. Each incident triggers a notification to local officials along with relevant imagery for timely investigations and enforcement.

name: Bournemouth, Christchurch & Poole Council monitors coastal water quality with AI sensors
desc: Council officials and Poole Harbour Commissioners worked with UnifAI to install AI-powered sensors on coastal buoys. UnifAI's platform turns raw data on water pollutants and industrial discharges into in-depth analyses of quality levels.

name: Bournemouth, Christchurch & Poole Councils turn litter maps into localized engagement
desc: Ellipsis Earth uses AI-enabled drones and local camera footage to track plastic litter patterns throughout the area. A map created during COVID-19 lockdown provides a relatively clean slate for future analysis. Multiple map layers allow council officials to customize bin placement and street cleaning routes.

name: British Standards Institution: EU AI Act Readiness Assessment and Algorithmic Auditing
desc: Organisations deploying advanced algorithmic systems face growing regulatory requirements under the EU AI Act, necessitating robust compliance, testing and documentation processes. Many lack structured methodologies to assess fairness, robustness and transparency.

name: Buckinghamshire Council: Early adoption of Microsoft Copilot
desc: Buckinghamshire Council became one of the first UK local authorities to adopt Microsoft Copilot in October 2023, granting early access to 300 staff across digital services, business support, customer service and other departments.

name: Caddy - AI powered tool for customer service functions  (part of the Humphrey toolkit)
authority: i.AI - Department for Science, Innovation, and Technology
desc: Caddy was piloted to support frontline customer service agents handling complex citizen enquiries under time pressure. Developed with Citizens Advice organisations, the objective was to improve response quality while reducing cognitive load on advisers.

name: Cambridgeshire County Council, GB pilots AI-powered traffic sensors at East Road in Cambridge
desc: Smart sensors are being trialed in Cambridge to make it safer for people to cross the road by using artificial intelligence to reduce waiting times for pedestrians and road users.

name: ChatGPT-powered GOV.UK chatbot on trial
desc: Citizens accessing GOV.UK often need to navigate large volumes of content to find relevant information about public services, benefits and regulations.

name: Chatbot for Collecting Patient Feedback
desc: The Royal United Hospital in Bath needed a more effective way to gather patient feedback without overloading staff or relying on low-response manual survey processes.

name: Chatbot for Mental Health and Wellbeing Support
desc: North Lanarkshire introduced this use case in response to rising suicide rates and the need for more accessible, immediate and low-barrier routes into mental health support.

name: Co-creation of a Data Charter for AI in the Camden Council
desc: Public authorities increasingly rely on data-driven technologies, raising concerns about transparency, accountability and community trust. Camden Council partnered with The Alan Turing Institute to co-create a Data Charter defining principles for ethical data collection, processing and sharing.

name: Computer vision e-scooter technology to be trialled in UK city
desc: The pilot is a UK trial of computer vision–enabled e-scooters designed to improve safety and urban mobility management in shared micromobility systems. The scooters are equipped with on-device AI and camera-based perception systems that can analyse the surrounding environment in real time.

name: Connect - AI to match capacity to demand in the Grid connections queue
authority: i.AI - Department for Science, Innovation, and Technology
desc: The transition to renewable energy is constrained by delays in connecting new projects to the electricity grid, creating long queues and uncertainty for investors. In the UK, grid operators require better tools to allocate limited capacity more effectively.

name: Consular Digital Triage - Automating consular enquiry responses
desc: British nationals abroad frequently contact consular services for urgent but routine issues such as lost passports, emergency travel documents, or eligibility for support, creating high volumes of written and telephone enquiries for the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO).

name: Consult - AI for public engagement (part of the Humphrey toolkit)
authority: i.AI - Department for Science, Innovation, and Technology
desc: Public consultations often generate thousands of written responses, making manual analysis slow, costly, and prone to inconsistency. UK policymakers need timely and comprehensive insights to inform decision-making while maintaining transparency and accountability.

name: ConsultAI: Bath and North East Somerset Council parking charge proposals
authority: Bath and North East Somerset Council
desc: When Bath and North East Somerset Council consulted on proposed parking-charge changes in 2024, it received more than 4,300 responses and over 18,000 free-text comments.

name: DVSA MOT -  Intelligent, data-driven approach to better target Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency (DVSA) resources
desc: The Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency (DVSA) needed a more effective way to prioritise inspections across a very large MOT testing ecosystem, covering 23,000 garages and 66,000 testers, at a time when examiner capacity was limited and manual targeting could not easily keep pace with the volume and complexity of…

name: Daisy - an AI "granny" that will waste scammers' time
desc: Daisy, a non-human “AI granny,” has been developed by the UK telecom operator Virgin Media O2 as an innovative tool to disrupt phone scammers.

name: DeepMiner: Transforming business support through data integration
authority: Scottish Government’s Directorate for Equality, Inclusion & Human Rights
desc: The Scottish Government identified a significant structural problem in the design and delivery of business support: information about businesses was fragmented across multiple organisations, making it difficult to generate a coherent view of need, target support effectively or evaluate outcomes across the public…

name: Derby City Council connects residents to city services with AI-powered digital assistants
desc: Since April visitors to Derby City Council’s website and those who call the council’s main phone line can seek help and assistance from AI “helpers”. Darcie can help with council services and Ali is available to help Derby Homes customers with housing enquiries.

name: Derby City Council embarks on next phase of using AI to streamline services
desc: The City Council is pioneering the use of AI technology in local government in partnership with ICS.AI, a leader in developing AI solutions in the public sector, and has now signed a £7 million contract to deliver the next stage of its project.

name: Developing a Generative AI platform for construction cost management
desc: The Futures of Systems, People and Projects (FUSP) laboratory has been awarded a £1.18m Innovate UK grant to produce a generative AI platform for boosting the productivity and accuracy of cost planning in construction. This new research project follows on from a successful feasibility study funded by Innovate UK.

name: Development of GenAI-based tool for education by gov.uk - "Building a proof of concept for Generative AI feedback and resource generation in education contexts"
desc: Teachers face substantial workload pressures linked to marking, feedback preparation and the creation of classroom resources, yet these tasks are central to maintaining teaching quality and supporting pupil progress.

name: Dorset Council leverages 5G connectivity along the coast for Aquaculture Monitoring System
desc: Council leaders and JET Engineering System are developing the system for a growing aquaculture sector. Underwater cameras and buoys made from sustainable materials monitor conditions at Jurassic Sea Farms in Portland Harbour.

name: Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council creates smart intersection with AI-powered road sensors
desc: Dudley Metropolitan Borough Council has begun during 2023 to deploy road sensors in an effort to improve traffic flows and reduce congestion.

name: EHPS - Early help profiling system to identify children and families considered vulnerable
desc: Hackney Council introduced the Early Help Profiling System to support earlier intervention for children and families considered vulnerable, in a context where public services were under pressure to identify risk sooner and target limited support resources more effectively.

name: EU Exit: ID document check - applying for settled status in the UK after Brexit
desc: Following the United Kingdom’s withdrawal from the European Union, millions of EU citizens needed to apply for settled status through a streamlined and scalable digital process.

name: FIRST - A Flexible Interactive Reading Support Tool
desc: The FIRST project uses innovative language technology to simplify documents for people with Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD).

name: Facial recognition Settled Status Applications - Checking identity
desc: As part of preparations for Brexit, the UK government launched a scheme to establish the residency rights of the estimated 3.4 million EU citizens living in the country.The registration system uses an the app checks identity through facial matching.

name: Facial recognition for apprehension police - Apprehension of suspects
desc: Police forces had begun trialing the use of automatic face recognition systems to automatically decide when people should be apprehended as suspects.

name: Foundry - Birmingham City
desc: Birmingham City Council launched the Foundry in 2023 to respond to a combination of budget pressure, rising service demand and the need to build stronger internal digital capability while reducing reliance on external consultants.

name: GCS Assist - Accelerating content creation for government communicators
desc: Government communicators must produce high-quality, timely content aligned with established standards and frameworks, often under tight deadlines. GCS Assist was developed in-house to support members of the UK Government Communication Service by accelerating routine content creation and review tasks.

name: GOV.UK App chatbot
authority: UK Government - Department of Science, Innovation and Technology
desc: Citizens often need to interact with multiple government services through separate websites and processes, making routine tasks time-consuming and difficult to navigate.

name: Gangs Violence Matrix (GVM) to predict crime in London
desc: Urban law enforcement agencies seek to identify individuals at risk of involvement in serious violence to inform prevention and safeguarding strategies. Since 2012, the Metropolitan Police has used the Gangs Violence Matrix to risk-assess individuals linked to gang activity.

name: Generative AI Transformation Project with Derby City Council and ICS.AI
desc: Municipal councils face increasing demand to deliver responsive, high-quality customer services while managing budget constraints and rising case complexity.

name: Greater Cambridge Shared Planning: AI-Driven Summarisation for Local Plan Consultations
desc: Greater Cambridge Shared Planning, a partnership between South Cambridgeshire District Council and Cambridge City Council, faced a substantial administrative burden in processing around 9,500 public comments for each Local Plan consultation.

name: HART - Assessment risk tool, predictive policing based on person data
desc: The Harm Assessment Risk Tool (HART) was introduced to support police decision-making by providing a structured assessment of an individual’s likelihood of future harm-related offending.

name: Harm Assessment Risk Tool (HART) in Durham
desc: Preliminary research into a two-year pilot programme run by Durham Constabulary, found the Harm Assessment Risk Tool (Hart) was slightly better overall at predicting reoffending rates than human custody sergeants.

name: Harvey - LLM for supporting contract analysis
desc: Harvey, the tool rolled out by Allen & Overy, apparently uses GPT-4 to help lawyers automate contract analysis, due diligence, conduct research, and generate insights, recommendations, and predictions across multiple practice areas.

name: Hello Lamp Post
desc: The Environment Agency is responsible for protecting communities from flood and coastal risks, yet engaging diverse local audiences and providing timely, location-specific safety information has been challenging through traditional communication channels.

name: Hertfordshire County Council implemented a AI-powered traffic monitoring platform
desc: County officials wanted a monitoring solution for automated and standardized data collection. Videos from local traffic cameras are sent through an app built on AWS Amplify to the AWS Rekognition tool for analysis. Traffic types, directions, and speeds are documented before image deletion.

name: Hertfordshire County Council: AI road maintenance robot
desc: Hertfordshire County Council, working with Robotiz3d and the University of Liverpool, set out to address a costly and persistent infrastructure problem: small cracks in roads are often left untreated until they develop into potholes, by which point repairs are more expensive, more disruptive and more damaging to road…

name: Hillingdon Council praised for innovative approach to safeguarding children
desc: With PwC and Amazon’s support, in only a three month period, Hillingdon became the first UK local authority to have deployed an automated voice and web chat solution at scale.

name: How DFID used satellite images to estimate populations
desc: DFID has deployed the programme in Nigeria, Zambia, Mozambique and Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). DFID has also conducted scoping missions to Tanzania, Ethiopia, and South Sudan.

name: How the Department for Transport used AI to improve MOT testing
desc: The DVSA applied a clustering model against garage test data from the last 3 months, as there was no labelled data available. The clustering model grouped MOT centres based on the behaviour they show when conducting MOT tests. The DVSA created a risk score for each garage in Great Britain.

name: How the Ministry of Justice used AI to compare prison reports
desc: The Ministry of Justice trained a neural network on the prison reports to track how people use specific words in prison contexts. The algorithm groups words with similar meanings to form an ‘intelligent search’ tool. New reports are automatically added to the tool’s library so the data remains up-to-date.

name: How we used deep learning to structure GOV.UK's content
desc: We used Natural Language Processing to make the text content on the page machine readable. We used this and the page metadata (like date published and department) to learn patterns that could be used to predict which sub-branches an untagged page should be organised in.

name: Humanising Authonomy - Behavioural AI to improve the safety of public transport
desc: Public transport and freight operators in London face a persistent road safety challenge in complex urban environments, where interactions between buses, heavy vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists, and other road users can change rapidly and create significant risk.

name: Humphrey -  AI tool to streamline public services, eliminate delays through improved data sharing, and reduce costs
authority: UK Government - Department of Science, Innovation and Technology
desc: Public services often suffer from fragmented data, repetitive administrative work, and slow internal processes, which can delay service delivery and reduce the time civil servants can spend on higher-value tasks.

name: Improving trackside worker safety
desc: Railway maintenance activities expose trackside workers to significant safety risks, particularly when operating near live rail environments. Network Rail is exploring geofencing technology as an additional safeguard to reinforce existing safety protocols.

name: Kent County Council: Using predictive analytics to prevent homelessness in Maidstone and Kent
desc: Kent County Council leveraged predictive analytics to identify individuals and households at risk of homelessness in Maidstone and across Kent.

name: Lancashire County Council – A strategic approach to deploying AI in transport
desc: Lancashire County Council is taking a structured approach to a persistent transport-management challenge: how to improve traffic flow, reduce congestion and make better use of existing infrastructure in a context of rising demand, constrained budgets and growing expectations for smarter mobility.

name: Leeds City Council pursues smart traffic management with AI for Detection technology
desc: The city has installed more than 180 AI for Detection sensors across 25 sites to tackle congestion thanks to the real-time detection of road users at junctions.

name: Leicester City Council  partners with university researchers on H2A: Lifestyle initiative
desc: Artificial intelligence is being used to develop personalised weight loss plans for people across Leicester in a new campaign to tackle obesity.

name: Lex - Simplifying Legislative Research (part of the Humphrey toolkit)
authority: i.AI - Department for Science, Innovation, and Technology
desc: Lex addressed the difficulty non-specialists face when researching complex legislation dispersed across statutes, amendments, and case law. The pilot targeted policymakers, legal advisers, and public servants needing fast, reliable legal insight.

name: Logo Detection and Classification Toolkit (LDK) - Automating the detection of unauthorised logo use on websites
desc: Unauthorised use of official government logos on fraudulent or misleading websites poses risks to citizens and undermines trust in public institutions. HM Revenue & Customs, working with central government partners, developed the Logo Detection and Classification Toolkit to automate the identification of such misuse.

name: London Borough of Redbridge modernizes planning requests and services with Planbot
desc: Planning services in the London Borough of Redbridge handle complex regulations and high volumes of enquiries, often diverting specialist staff from higher-value work. Residents and developers require clear guidance on planning rules, applications, and documentation.

name: London Electric Vehicle Charge Points Dashboard
desc: Electric Vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure - a vital component of London’s smart and green agenda - is being delivered by a wide range of public and private bodies across London (up to 50).

name: London Police Facial Recognition System
desc: The Metropolitan Police Service in London seeks to enhance its capacity to identify individuals of interest in public spaces in order to prevent crime, safeguard vulnerable persons and support ongoing investigations.

name: London TravelBot
desc: Transports for London created an automated service on Facebook Messenger to help you check the status of your Tube, rail or bus route. The service is free and uses latest data. The status checker is available for all Tube lines, DLR, London Overground, TfL Rail, trams and all bus routes.

name: Machine Learning towards a greener grid
desc: The “Towards a Greener Grid” project highlights how the Turing Institute collaborated with the National Grid Electricity System Operator to develop advanced data-driven forecasting models for renewable energy, particularly solar and wind power.

name: Magic Notes - Assisting social care workers through transcription and note-taking
desc: Social care professionals spend a significant proportion of their time on administrative documentation, reducing the time available for direct engagement with clients and contributing to workload pressure and burnout.

name: Manchester uses artificial intelligence to gain more insight into active travel
desc: City regions face increasing pressure to promote walking and cycling while ensuring that investments in active travel infrastructure are evidence-based.

name: Manchester’s Research & Intelligence Database - Identifying troubled families
desc: Manchester City Council is using a system it calls the Manchester Research & Intelligence Database to identify Troubled Families, families in need of support, to enable caseworkers to access more information more quickly than previously and to enable the collection and analysis of data to assess services and impact.

name: Mapping mangroves with Serverless and Deep Learning
desc: Global mangrove mapping relied on infrequently updated datasets that could not capture the dynamic changes affecting these critical coastal ecosystems, limiting understanding of carbon sequestration, biodiversity, and natural coastal protection.

name: Mia - Streamlining breast cancer screening with AI
desc: Breast cancer screening programmes face growing demand while radiology departments experience workforce shortages and increasing workloads, which can affect screening throughput and consistency.

name: Minute - AI transcription service (part of the Humphrey toolkit)
authority: i.AI - Department for Science, Innovation, and Technology
desc: Minute was piloted to reduce the administrative burden of documenting meetings across public services, where manual note-taking and transcription consume significant staff time. Public servants and administrative teams were the primary users, seeking accurate and secure summaries.

name: Mobile-Age
desc: The Mobile-Age project focused on open government data, mobile technology, and the provision of public services addressing the needs of Europe's elderly population. Researchers used a co-creation approach for services related to the production and use of open data for cities.

name: Monitoring slavery from space
desc: Brick kilns across the South Asian “Brick Belt” are associated with high prevalence of forced labour, yet the absence of reliable data on their number and distribution has hindered effective intervention by governments and non-governmental organisations.

name: Monmouthshire County Council  monitors the success of new bike lanes with Vivacity Labs platform
desc: Council officials approved protected contraflow bike lanes on one-way streets in three towns. Vivacity Labs sensors were installed at three points on Lion Street in Abergavenny for ongoing evaluation of lane impacts.

name: NHS AI test spots tiny cancers missed by doctors
desc: Early detection of breast cancer significantly improves treatment outcomes, yet subtle abnormalities in mammograms can be difficult to identify consistently. The NHS piloted a diagnostic support tool alongside clinicians to assess its effectiveness in analysing breast screening images.

name: NHS Flu and COVID-19 Vaccines Chatbot
desc: The ‘NHS Winter Vaccines Virtual Helper' turned one search into a conversation.

name: National Data Analytics Solution (NDAS)
desc: The National Data Analytics Solution was developed by West Midlands Police in collaboration with the UK Home Office and other forces to enhance early identification of individuals considered at risk of serious violence.

name: New AI-Powered Cameras Spot Distracted Drivers in the UK
desc: Road safety authorities in the United Kingdom face persistent risks from distracted driving and seatbelt non-compliance, contributing to preventable accidents and injuries.

name: North Yorkshire Council: Using AI to reimagine Children’s Social Care
desc: North Yorkshire Council is exploring how to improve children’s social care in a service environment where case complexity, workload pressures and the need for timely, well-informed decisions place heavy demands on professionals.

name: Northumberland County Council- FloodAI, using AI to detect flash floods
desc: Northumberland County Council launched FloodAI to address a serious public-safety and resilience issue: flash floods can develop rapidly, leaving little time for authorities and communities to respond.

name: Offender Assessment System (OASys)
desc: The Offender Assessment System was developed by the Ministry of Justice to standardise risk and needs assessment across probation services and prisons in England and Wales.

name: OrQA - Organ Quality Assessment - the technology scans images of organs to look at suitability for kidney and liver transplant
desc: Organ transplantation depends on rapid and accurate assessment of donor organs, yet decisions about suitability are complex and time-sensitive, and clinicians must often judge quality under conditions of uncertainty.

name: PROTEUS (Scalable online machine learning for predictive analytics and real-time visualisation)
desc: PROTEUS mission was to investigate and develop ready-to-use scalable online machine learning algorithms and interactive visualization techniques for real-time predictive analytics to deal with extremely large data sets and data streams.

name: Parlex - Forecasting Parliamentary Reactions (part of the Humphrey toolkit)
authority: i.AI - Department for Science, Innovation, and Technology
desc: Parlex was piloted to help policy teams anticipate parliamentary responses to proposed legislation, addressing the challenge of navigating vast volumes of historical debate and political positioning.

name: Peterborough City Council: Hey Geraldine, a personalised AI assistant
desc: Peterborough City Council introduced “Hey Geraldine” to improve how residents access information and guidance from the council, particularly in situations where generic web content or traditional contact routes may not provide a quick or sufficiently tailored response.

name: Pioneering Use of Microsoft Copilot - Barnsley Council
desc: Barnsley Council introduced Microsoft Copilot to tackle a familiar public-sector challenge: high volumes of administrative work that consume staff time and reduce capacity for more meaningful, citizen-facing tasks.

name: PlaceBuilder - Unlocking community-driven development
desc: Hanwood Park, one of the UK’s largest planned housing developments, required an approach to consultation that could keep local communities involved throughout a complex and long-term planning process.

name: Pothole ROBOT hits the roads in Hertfordshire
desc: Local highway authorities face persistent challenges from potholes, which damage vehicles, increase accident risk and generate high maintenance costs through labour-intensive repair processes.

name: Powys County Council builds AI-enabled system for expedited Fuel Support Scheme reviews
desc: The council's developers spent a year designing a platform for automated reviews of local applications to the national support program. Applicants meeting all of the scheme's criteria received automatic approvals from the system.

name: Project-A.I.R (Artificial Intelligence Guided Retrofit)
desc: The project, known as Project-A.I.R (Artificial Intelligence Guided Retrofit), is the first AI-enabled concept to deliver proven efficiencies in the field of housing decarbonisation.

name: Redbox - Bringing Generative AI to the way the Civil Service works
authority: UK Government - Department of Science, Innovation and Technology
desc: Civil servants work with large volumes of briefings, letters, speeches, meeting minutes, and other documents, and much of their time can be absorbed by locating key information, summarising content, and drafting routine material.

name: Resource Allocation System
desc: Adult social care authorities must translate assessed needs into indicative budgets in a way that is fair, transparent, and flexible enough to reflect individual circumstances, while still allowing professional judgement and support planning to shape the final outcome.

name: Review Automoderation Tool - Automating content moderation on NHS.UK
authority: Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) / NHS England (NHSE)
desc: NHS.UK receives around 100,000 user reviews each year, all of which must comply with strict moderation policies on personal data, abuse, discrimination, and safeguarding.

name: Robin AI - LLM for supporting Legals
desc: RobinAI is a legal industry platform that uses Large Language Models (LLMs), including Anthropic's model "Claude to automate tasks such as reading, writing, and editing text data.

name: Robots to be used in UK care homes to help reduce loneliness
desc: Loneliness and social isolation are persistent challenges in residential care homes, particularly among older adults with limited mobility or family contact. A UK pilot explored whether social robots could complement care staff by providing companionship and daily interaction for residents.

name: SAM - Service AI Assistant Module - Streamlining routine queries through AI-powered contact centre tools
desc: Local authorities receive high volumes of routine enquiries about services such as waste collection, council tax and basic administrative procedures, placing sustained pressure on contact centres and frontline staff. Residents increasingly expect immediate, round-the-clock access to information.

name: SCRIPT Project - Supervised Care & Rehabilitation Involving Personal Tele-robotics
desc: The SCRIPT project was created to address a major challenge in stroke rehabilitation: how to ensure that patients, particularly those in the chronic phase of recovery, can continue to receive intensive and repetitive therapy beyond the clinical setting.

name: Scout - AI-powered tool to improve government major project delivery
authority: i.AI - Department for Science, Innovation, and Technology and Infrastructure and Projects Authority (IPA)
desc: Oversight of major government projects in the United Kingdom requires the analysis of extensive documentation, often under time pressure and with high financial stakes.

name: Sheffield City Council works with VivaCity on AI-powered monitoring of its Clean Air Zone
desc: City officials introduced a CAZ for high-emission commercial vehicles in February 2023. A three-year monitoring agreement with VivaCity gathers data from 17 sensors. The AI-enabled sensors track traffic patterns on the A61 for analysis of peak and off-peak periods.

name: SignPort: Transforming access to BSL interpreters through technology
authority: Scottish Government’s Directorate for Equality, Inclusion & Human Rights
desc: Access to British Sign Language interpreters is essential for Deaf BSL users to participate fully in work, healthcare, public services and social life, yet existing booking systems are often fragmented, inefficient and unable to match users with available interpreters reliably.

name: Simplyhealth supports their digital transformation with PolyAI
desc: Simplyhealth, a leading UK health insurer, partnered with PolyAI to develop a customer-led voice assistant aimed at modernising their customer service operations. The voice assistant efficiently handles common FAQs and identifies vulnerable callers, directing them to appropriate departments for personalised support.

name: Smart sENsor Devices fOr rehabilitation and Connected health - SENDoc
desc: SENDoc introduces the use of wearable sensor systems in ageing communities in northern UK remote areas. These sensors can measure mobility, strength, balance, and also wellbeing, exercise, and safety, and have the potential to support independent living.

name: South Cambridgeshire - Contact centre chatbot to improve resident satisfaction
desc: South Cambridgeshire District Council deployed a contact-centre chatbot to address a common local-government challenge: high volumes of routine enquiries can slow response times, reduce service efficiency and leave staff with less capacity to deal with complex or sensitive cases.

name: St Helens Borough Council – augmenting TEC with AI
desc: St Helens Council launched its Technology Enabled Care Hub in 2024 as part of its 2024–2027 Adult Social Care strategy and wider “reablement – home first” approach, responding to the challenge of supporting people more proactively after hospital discharge and helping them regain confidence in everyday life.

name: Staffordshire County Council implemented AI technology for road assessments
desc: The county's highways team previously used manual inspections and ReportIt submissions for assessments. Highway inspectors now use the Vaisala RoadAI tool on their mobile devices for ongoing evaluations of road conditions.

name: Strategic spatial planning: inclusive engagement and AI in strategic spatial planning
authority: Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government (MHCLG)
desc: In 2020 and 2021, the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government commissioned a large-scale digital consultation across the Oxford-Cambridge Arc, a region spanning five counties and 3.3 million residents, to inform the development of a long-term Spatial Framework.

name: Stroke AI - Interpreting brain scans with AI to improve outcomes for stroke patients
authority: Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) / NHS England (NHSE)
desc: Stroke treatment is extremely time-sensitive, and delays in diagnosis can have severe consequences for patient outcomes. Stroke AI was introduced across England to support clinical teams in rapidly interpreting brain scans and making treatment decisions.

name: Sunderland City Council converts data into improved services with AI-powered platform
desc: Sunderland in north-east England is implementing a new data platform to inform action on issues such as anti-social behaviour, social care, health, and environmental incidents.

name: Swindon Borough Council: Simply Readable, an AI easy-read solution
desc: Swindon Borough Council developed Simply Readable to tackle a significant accessibility gap in public communication: producing Easy-Read documents for residents with learning disabilities can be slow, expensive and difficult to scale, even though accessible information is essential for fair access to public services.

name: System replacing final examinations in a pattern following previous years
authority: Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation (Ofqual)
desc: Automated decision-making system deployed by the Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation (Ofqual) on the basis of an data-based assessment to replace A-level examinations as wells as General Certificates of Secondary Education i 2020 and replacing International Baccalaureate (IB) final examinations in…

name: The City of Edinburgh Council continues smart city evolution with CCTV Control Centre
desc: The new Control Centre will see the provision of high-definition CCTV cameras, expanded security coverage, and the introduction of advanced analytics and artificial intelligence that can provide situational awareness and predict and alert new and existing threats.

name: The Family Hub in Halton Borough Council: Digital front door in family hub services
desc: Families seeking support often need timely, clear and accessible information, yet service pathways can be difficult to navigate, especially outside standard working hours.

name: TravelBot - Chatbot for travel information
desc: Transport for London launched TravelBot to address a common customer-service problem in urban transport: passengers often need immediate answers about bus arrivals, service disruptions and route information, yet traditional service channels can be slower, less convenient or harder to access during travel.

name: Tunbridge Wells Borough Council: The Amelia Scott, Collecting Tomorrow
desc: At The Amelia Scott cultural hub, Tunbridge Wells Borough Council sought to address two linked challenges: preserving historical artefacts more efficiently and creating richer ways for visitors and local communities to engage with collections.

name: U.K. to use AI to spot dangerous side effects in the COVID-19 vaccinations
authority: U.K. Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)
desc: Large-scale vaccination programmes generate vast volumes of safety reports that regulators must review to identify potential adverse effects and protect public health.

name: Voice assistant services
desc: Aylesbury Vale District Council sought to expand digital access to local government information by offering residents an alternative to web-based and telephone enquiries. The objective was to improve convenience and accessibility for routine questions relating to council services, payments and waste management.

name: Wandsworth Borough Council tracks air quality and traffic patterns with Eco Census cameras
desc: The AI-powered cameras measure common pollutants including nitrogen dioxide (NO2) and particulate matter (PM) in real time, including previously unmeasured PM2.5s. A better monitoring of air pollution is a key part of the council’s new Air Quality Action Plan.

name: Warm Home Discount Energy Cost Predictor - Modelling energy costs to determine eligibility for Warm Home Discount scheme
authority: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ)
desc: Identifying households eligible for energy cost support is complex, particularly when relying on self-application processes that disadvantage less informed or vulnerable citizens. The Warm Home Discount Energy Cost Predictor was developed to improve targeting of support under the UK’s Warm Home Discount scheme.

name: Warwickshire County Council: “Access to Food” – exploring LLMs for citizen needs
desc: Warwickshire County Council developed the “Access to Food” project to better understand how residents, particularly those living in deprived areas, access healthy and affordable food options.

name: Westminster City Council deploys AI-supported cameras in campaign against illegal dumping
desc: The city installed CCTV cameras connected to an AI-enabled platform at three illegal dumping hotspots. Each camera records nearby license plates during suspected illegal dumping incidents.

name: Wigan Council: QuickAction in adult social care
desc: Wigan Council introduced QuickAction to address a pressing operational issue in adult social care: professionals were spending substantial time on repetitive administrative tasks, reducing the time available for direct support to residents.

name: YPO, Procurement Information Provider
desc: YPO has introduced a chatbot - the Procurement Information Provider (PIP) to help public sector buyers navigate their way through YPO's services and discover the frameworks on offer. The chatbot can provide information from other areas of the website and direct users to relevant procurement teams.

name: Virtual St. Peter's Basilica with Artificial Intelligence
desc: Historic and religious landmarks are often difficult to document, interpret, and open up fully to the public, especially in areas that are physically inaccessible or too fragile for close everyday access. The digital twin of St.
